title: Light Canvas
subtitle: An interactive drawing system
imageAlt: Three genuine Light Canvas application screens showing drawing controls and session statistics
imageCaption: Application screens from the Light Canvas project.
summary: Turning a flat surface into an interactive drawing space through computer vision and IoT.
problem: Interactive educational tools can require dedicated computing devices. Light Canvas explores a portable alternative for drawing and learning.
contribution: I developed an end-to-end system integrating visual tracking, sensing, image processing, application software, and real-time interaction.
methods: Python, OpenCV, image processing, IoT, Flutter
outcome: The work was published at ACM ICCA 2024.

title: AutoML for air quality & disease burden
subtitle: Looking beyond random-split evaluation
imageAlt: System architecture from the AutoML project report showing data collection, preprocessing, modeling, and evaluation
imageCaption: Authentic system architecture from the project report.
summary: Examining environmental and health data, with attention to generalization across countries.
problem: Predictive performance on randomly split data may conceal failures when a model is applied in a different setting.
contribution: I developed a machine-learning framework and examined country-grouped validation to expose generalization weaknesses, motivating revised evaluation and SHAP-based interpretation.
methods: Python, AutoML, SHAP, grouped validation, distribution-shift analysis
outcome: An analysis and evaluation framework documented in my latest CV. This prototype is separate from peer-reviewed publications.

title: Autonomous delivery bot
subtitle: A line-following robotics prototype
summary: A small delivery prototype that follows a predefined line, combining embedded control and cargo transport.
problem: A delivery task can be a practical way to connect sensing, control, mechanics, and reliable movement along a known route.
contribution: I developed a prototype with a cargo chamber and line-following sensors, using Arduino and embedded control to follow a predefined path.
methods: Arduino, line-following sensors, embedded control, IoT
outcome: A working delivery-bot prototype documented in my earlier CV. This is line-following autonomy; broader navigation capabilities are not claimed.
imageAlt: AI-generated concept illustration of a small delivery robot carrying a box along a marked line
imageCaption: AI-generated concept illustration; the actual prototype photograph will replace it.

title: Adaptive mobile-banking interfaces
subtitle: Personalization with human-centered evaluation
summary: Using interaction behavior to adapt a mobile-banking interface.
problem: A fixed mobile interface may not suit the needs and interaction patterns of every user.
contribution: I developed and evaluated a machine-learning-driven adaptive interface using user behavior, combining predictive modeling, clustering, SHAP-based explanation, and human-centered evaluation.
methods: Machine learning, clustering, SHAP, adaptive interfaces, statistical evaluation
imageAlt: AI-generated concept illustration of mobile interfaces adapting to interaction patterns
imageCaption: AI-generated concept illustration; not the published app interface.

title: Web3 vs Web2 user experience & PLS-SEM tool
subtitle: Comparative UX research and analysis tooling
summary: A prototype-based comparison of user experience in decentralized and conventional social media.
problem: Decentralized social platforms introduce interaction choices that need to be evaluated from users’ perspectives.
contribution: I designed a prototype to evaluate UX differences between Web3 and Web2 social platforms. This work also includes a PLS-SEM tool, as part of the Web3/Web2 paper.
methods: Comparative HCI evaluation, prototyping, System Usability Scale, PLS-SEM tool
outcome: Accepted and presented at HCI-E 2025; the paper is in press for Springer CCIS. Detailed documentation of the analysis tool and a public software link will be added when available.

imageCaption: AI-generated concept illustration of analysis tooling; not a screenshot or study result.

title: Multimodal multi-agent AI
subtitle: Reasoning together, checking the evidence
summary: Specialized agents that share multimodal evidence and verify intermediate reasoning.
problem: An unreliable intermediate answer can propagate through a multi-agent workflow and shape later decisions.
contribution: I am developing a LangGraph-based framework in which specialized agents process evidence, exchange context, coordinate reasoning, and perform cross-agent verification.
methods: Python, LangGraph, multimodal evidence, agent coordination, failure analysis
outcome: Ongoing research on information sharing, verification, and error propagation. No benchmark improvements or completed evaluation results are claimed.
imageAlt: AI-generated concept illustration of specialized agent modules sharing multimodal evidence through a central notebook
imageCaption: AI-generated concept illustration; not the implemented system architecture or an experimental result.

title: LLM & VLM trust comparison
subtitle: Confidence, explanations, and human reliance
summary: Investigating how uncertainty and high-confidence errors shape trust in language and multimodal models.
problem: A confident answer can appear convincing even when it is wrong. Appropriate reliance requires more than persuasive language.
contribution: I am investigating how model confidence, uncertainty communication, explanations, and high-confidence errors influence human reliance on LLMs and VLMs.
methods: Human-centered evaluation, comparative model analysis, uncertainty and trust calibration
outcome: Ongoing investigation. Comparative findings and study materials will be shared once available.

imageCaption: AI-generated concept illustration; not a user-study finding or a model comparison result.

title: Trustworthy skin-lesion classification
subtitle: Uncertainty and explanation in medical vision
summary: Studying how medical-image models can communicate uncertainty and support careful human review.
problem: A classifier’s prediction alone does not explain when its output may be unreliable or how a clinician should interpret it.
contribution: I am developing a DINO-ViT-based framework on HAM10000, incorporating uncertainty quantification, visual explanations, fairness analysis, and clinician-centered evaluation.
methods: DINO-ViT, HAM10000, uncertainty quantification, visual explanations, fairness analysis
outcome: Ongoing research. Final performance, clinical validation, and deployment outcomes have not been established.
